rights.worldwide: to confirm: death dates of every author, translator and editor named (life + 70 years); Godet died 1900; A. Cusin, the translator, to confirm

notes: Not on CCEL; the text is archive.org djvu OCR of the 1881 printing of both volumes (Vol. I: commentaryonstp01cusigoog; Vol. II: commentaryonstp00cusigoog, https://archive.org/details/commentaryonstp00cusigoog). The Introduction is not used. Entries cover Godet's comments on Romans 1:1-16:24, verse by verse as he arranges them ("Ver. 6.", "Vv. 1, 2.", "Vv. 17-20."); each unit opens with Godet's own rendering of the verse as printed. Where a passage or sub-section ("FOURTH PASSAGE (I. 18-32)", "Vv. 7-13.") opens with an introduction before the first verse mark, that introduction is an entry on the passage's range (or its first verse, joined to the first note when short). General introductions under the larger divisions (Preface, Treatise, Part, Section headings), the section titles themselves, and Godet's excursus on the critical question of the doxology are left out. Godet's notes on 16:25-27 are left out: the Open Word Bible text has no Romans 16:25-27. Long notes are cut at sentence ends into entries of up to about 350-400 words; ' ...' at the start or end of an entry marks such a cut. Dropped: running heads, page numbers, signature lines, the translator's and author's footnotes (mostly textual variants), and footnote markers (the OCR's ^ and *). Greek: the OCR turns Godet's many Greek words into Latin-letter garbage (e.g. "SovXo^", "vofiov", "Oeov"); nothing was retyped. Garbled Greek words and phrases were left out and the cut marked ' ... ', parentheses holding only garbled Greek were dropped, and sentences made up mostly of garbled Greek were replaced by ' ... '. The detection was by script and errs toward cutting: some English words badly misread by the OCR were also cut, and a few short garbled Greek words may remain (e.g. "elfu", "epya"). Godet's verse renderings are printed in italics, which the OCR garbles more than roman type (e.g. "as lanff as he liveth t"); they are kept as read, with only garbled words cut. OCR slips are otherwise left as printed by the scan, apart from the corrections in library/corrections/godet-romans.json (God for "Ood", "Grod", "Gk)d"; Rome/Roman(s) for "Bome", "Borne", "Boman"; from for "&om", "fix)m"; and a few others). Left uncorrected, among many: "ia" (is/in), "tiie", "bat" (but), "imder", "OentUes", "evU", "t" and "f" for question marks, "w." for vv., old-style figures read as letters in references ("xiL", "viiL"), and "T. B." for T. R. In Vol. II a few pages are badly scanned, and a few footnotes on textual variants that the OCR set inside the text may remain (e.g. the notes on xv. 4-6 and xv. 20, 21). Headings are Godet's short lemmas where 12 words or fewer, otherwise empty. Chapter and verse placement was read from Godet's verse marks; a handful of OCR-misread verse numbers (e.g. "Vv. 18, 14" for 13, 14; "Yv. 1.4, 15" for 14, 15) were set by hand.
